article.articleHeadline: പകർച്ചവ്യാധി മരണങ്ങളിൽ പകുതിയും എലിപ്പനി മൂലം; സ്വയംചികിത്സ ആപത്ത്, കരുതൽവേണം
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Half of deaths from infectious diseases are due to smallpox; self-medication is dangerous, caution is needed.
article.articleSummary: Smallpox now accounts for more than half of Kerala's infectious-disease deaths, with two recent fatalities in Ernakulam and Kozhikode. In the first week of this month, six smallpox deaths have been recorded. Dr. A. Althaf, Professor at Thiruvananthapuram Medical College, says annual smallpox deaths run about 300–400 over the last five years, and early treatment can avert most deaths. A 2025 analysis found 36.72% of smallpox deaths among daily-wage workers; monsoon exposure in muddy water is a major risk. Other affected groups include agricultural workers (10.94%), domestic gardening (10.16%), construction (9.38%), and laborers (7.81%). Transmission occurs through water/soil contaminated with urine and excreta of elephants, donkeys, cats, dogs, and cattle, entering via skin wounds or mucous membranes. Symptoms: sudden high fever, severe headache, muscle pain, dizziness, limb pain, eye redness, jaundice, and yellow urine. Prophylaxis with weekly doxycycline (200 mg) per doctor's advice for high-risk individuals. Self-medication dangerous.

triage.headline_ja: 感染症死亡の半数はレプトスピラ症（エリパンニ）が原因。自己判断による治療は危険、注意が必要

triage.notes: Bluedotの疾患タグ『Smallpox（天然痘）』は誤り。記事内容はレプトスピラ症(Leptospirosis)についてであり、動物の尿・排泄物で汚染された水や土壌からの感染、ドキシサイクリンによる予防投与など典型的なレプトスピラ症の説明。ケララ州で毎年モンスーン期に発生する既知の風土病であり、国際的な異常性・拡大リスクは低い。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria spreads its reach in Surguja: 39 positive patients found in the Udaipur area, all from the Hill Korwa and Pando tribes.
article.articleSummary: 39 Plasmodium falciparum malaria cases confirmed in the Udaipur area of Surguja district, Chhattisgarh, India. All infections are Pf malaria; most patients belong to the Hill Korwa and Pando tribes. Affected villages include Mataringa, Kharranagar, Mushardand, Mukna Par, Baro Par, Bakoi, and Semi Ghoghra. Health authorities have intensified surveillance with house-to-house surveys and rapid diagnostic tests; positive patients are started on radical treatment immediately to prevent severe illness. Mosquito-net distribution is prioritized in affected households, and field teams are conducting ongoing camps to identify suspected cases, test, and provide treatment. Residents are urged to seek testing for fever or malaria-like symptoms and to adopt vector-control measures against mosquitoes. The report does not mention any fatalities.

article.articleHeadline: Bakti Indonesia 2026 Soroti Tantangan Pengobatan TBC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bakti Indonesia 2026 Spotlights the Challenges in TB Treatment
article.articleSummary: TB remains Indonesia’s major infectious-disease burden, highlighted at Bakti Indonesia 2026 in Semarang, Central Java (Aug 6–8, 2026) at Kelenteng Agung Sam Poo Kong. Indonesia ranks second globally for TB, with about 1,080,000 new cases and 125,000 deaths annually (~14 daily deaths). Transmission is airborne from active pulmonary TB; incubation is 1.5–2 months, and roughly 5% of exposed become ill, while most remain dormant for decades. Pulmonary TB treatment lasts at least six months with periodic clinical and radiographic monitoring; extrapulmonary TB such as lymph node TB requires 9–12 months. Emphasis is on early detection and full treatment adherence to prevent resistance. The event also delivered donor blood education and blood-pressure guidance, benefiting around 5,000 residents.

article.articleHeadline: കാഞ്ചിയാറിൽ മലേറിയ പടരുന്നു; 14 പേർക്ക് രോഗബാധ, രണ്ടു മരണം | കാഞ്ചിയാറിൽ മലേറിയ പടരുന്നു; 14 പേർക്ക് രോഗബാധ, രണ്ടു മരണം
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria spreading in Kanchiyar; 14 people infected, two deaths.
article.articleSummary: As of 8 August 2026, malaria is spreading in Kanchiyar panchayat, within Kattappana region of Kerala, affecting more than 2,000 interstate migrant workers living in makeshift sheds with inadequate sanitation. Fourteen malaria cases have been confirmed, including two deaths. Additionally, five people are reported with another illness described as 'manthuroga disease' and four are HIV positive. The outbreak appears concentrated among interstate laborers, with no precise headcounts or reliable facility data for the workers. Many shelter centers lack basic amenities like toilets, and employers/agents have been unwilling to provide accurate numbers to authorities. Left party leaders are demanding more health personnel, funds, and vehicles to strengthen prevention and treatment, accusing the panchayat administration of negligence and propaganda. If preventive actions do not improve, the LDF threatens protests. Leaders P. J. Sathyapalan, Jose Njarakkulam, K.C. Biju, Baji Gopal, K.P. Saji, and Abhilash Matthew spoke at the press conference.

triage.headline_ja: カンチヤールでマラリアが拡大、14人感染、2人死亡
triage.triage_reason: 移民労働者コミュニティでマラリアが拡大し死亡例も発生、衛生環境不良による継続的曝露と流行しやすさがあり、地元政治勢力からの対応要求(社会的関心)も見られるためフルRRAでの確認が望ましい。
triage.notes: ケララ州カンチヤール地区の移民労働者コミュニティにおける局地的マラリア流行。衛生設備不足の仮設住居に2000人以上が居住し、14人感染・2人死亡・HIV陽性者4人も報告。地元政党(LDF)が行政の不作為を批判し、抗議活動を示唆しているため政治的関心は高いが、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは確認されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Is contaminated water making people sicker during monsoon? Doctor explains rising risk of Diarrhoea, Typhoid and Hepatitis
article.articleSummary: New Delhi monsoon floods and overflowing drains raise sewage contamination of drinking-water sources, increasing risk of diarrhoea, vomiting and GI infections. Dr. Prashant Sinha notes rises in diarrhoea, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, cholera and related illnesses during the monsoon. Contaminated water can enter the food chain via washing, ice-making and food preparation, with unsafe household water storage and handling adding to risk. Illnesses linked to contaminated water include diarrhoeal diseases from E. coli, Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, norovirus, rotavirus, Giardia and Cryptosporidium; cholera (Vibrio cholerae); typhoid (Salmonella Typhi); hepatitis A and E. Symptoms range from loose stools, cramps, nausea, vomiting, fever and fatigue to jaundice for hepatitis; dehydration is the major danger. Water may look/smell normal, so chlorination or boiling after flooding is advised. Persistent diarrhoea warrants medical consultation.

triage.headline_ja: モンスーン期の汚染水は人々をより病気にしているのか？下痢・腸チフス・肝炎のリスク上昇について医師が解説
triage.triage_reason: 特定の発生事例の報告ではなく、モンスーン期における一般的な水系感染症リスクに関する医師の一般的な健康啓発記事であり、具体的な症例数や集団発生の報告がないため。
triage.notes: 記事は特定のアウトブレイク事例ではなく、モンスーン期における水系感染症全般（コレラ、腸チフス、A型/E型肝炎等）のリスクについての医師による一般的な健康アドバイス記事。具体的な症例数・発生地域の特定報告なし。

article.articleHeadline: Monkey Attacks Spark Panic in Indonesian City, Leaving 18 Injured
article.articleSummary: Rabies risk spurred after a monkey attacked 19 times in a city in Indonesia, injuring 18 people including children and the elderly; one victim was bitten twice. Junaid Ismail, head of the fire and rescue service in Tembilahan, confirmed to AFP that 18 injuries were linked to the incidents. Several wounds were serious, requiring more than 10 stitches, and doctors administered anti-rabies treatment due to bite exposure. The captured monkey was taken to Pekanbaru, the capital of Riau province on Sumatra, to be examined by the wildlife protection agency. Fears of additional attacks prompted the closure of 40 schools in the area, with hundreds of students instructed to attend classes online for three days while the emergency persists.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシアの都市で猿の襲撃が相次ぎパニック、18人負傷
triage.triage_reason: 野生の猿による異常な連続襲撃で18人が負傷し狂犬病曝露治療が行われ、学校閉鎖など地域社会への影響と関心が高いため、WPRO基準（異常性・重症度）とsocio-political関心の両方に該当する。
triage.notes: 米国・フロリダ等の発生地域情報はBluedotの誤付与と判断し除外。狂犬病自体のヒト-ヒト感染リスクはないが、野生動物由来の咬傷多発と地域パニック・学校閉鎖という社会的影響から一次スクリーニングでは注視対象とした。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Africa CDC, WHO urge stronger community response
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo accelerates, prompting Africa CDC and WHO to call for a stepped-up, community-led response. Uganda’s outbreak, ended July 28 with 20 cases and 2 deaths, is cited as a model for early detection, rapid contact tracing, community engagement, and cross-border surveillance. In DRC, Ituri Province remains the epicenter, with 3,973 confirmed cases, 1,801 deaths, and 776 recoveries across 51 health zones as of August 4; 99 new cases and 52 deaths were recorded in the prior 24 hours. A Bunia visit noted insecurity, misinformation, weak infrastructure, and medical-supply shortages; Rwangole Ebola Treatment Centre was inspected. Only 75% of identified contacts are monitored (target 95%), while North Kivu treatment centers run at 139% capacity. Authorities urge strengthened early detection, expanded lab and treatment capacity, improved infection prevention, timely frontline worker pay/protection, and sustained financing without travel restrictions.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：アフリカCDCとWHOが地域社会主導の対応強化を要請
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の感染拡大が続いており（確定例3,973例、死亡1,801例）、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数項目に該当し、国際的関心・支援の必要性も高いためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダの流行は7月28日に終息（20例・死亡2例）と報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。DRC・イトゥリ州が引き続き震源地であり、接触者追跡率が目標未達（75%/目標95%）、治療センターが定員139%で稼働するなど深刻な状況。

article.articleHeadline: 香港首现儿童染流感亡病例 专家警示"三疫夹击
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hong Kong reports its first pediatric influenza death; experts warn of a triple-epidemic onslaught.
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong reports its first pediatric influenza death of the year as authorities warn of a triple-epidemic involving COVID-19, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). A seven-year-old boy died on August 4 after an Influenza A infection that led to shock and brain injury despite receiving the seasonal flu vaccine, marking the year’s first pediatric flu fatality in Hong Kong. Pediatric infectious disease expert Guan Rihua says the death is an unfortunate but isolated event and urges continued vaccination confidence, noting antibody levels wane over time. He also calls for clarification of the child’s possible underlying conditions and whether the circulating flu strain has major mutations. Influenza is currently the most active pathogen; RSV commonly causes croup and pneumonia, and COVID-19 can trigger wheezing in children. To address the surge, Hong Kong’s Department of Health has purchased about 1.3 million vaccine doses from Sanofi, Sinovac, and AstraZeneca across four vaccines, with vaccination arrangements underway.

triage.headline_ja: 香港で今年初の小児インフルエンザ死亡例、専門家は「三重流行」の到来を警告
triage.triage_reason: 香港で季節性インフルエンザ・RSV・COVID-19の「三重流行」が懸念され、当局がワクチン確保など対応を進めており、社会的・行政的関心が高いためフルRRAでの確認が望ましい。
triage.notes: 専門家は本件を「孤立した不幸な事例」と評価しており、地域的流行拡大の証拠は現時点で限定的。香港衛生署によるワクチン確保など季節性対策が進行中であり、続報を注視する価値がある。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية توصي بإدراج لقاح "أرفيبو" في تجربة سريرية لمواجهة إيبولا بالكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO recommends including the Ervebo vaccine in a clinical trial to combat Ebola in Congo.
article.articleSummary: WHO technical advisory group recommends prioritizing the Ervebo vaccine (licensed for Ebola Zaire) for inclusion in a randomized clinical trial as part of efforts to curb the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Preliminary animal studies suggest cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, but human efficacy remains unproven and requires clinical confirmation. Using the vaccine to immunize contacts of infected individuals does not raise safety concerns while awaiting further efficacy data against Bundibugyo. The organization emphasizes that a vaccine tailored to Bundibugyo remains the best long-term option for this virus, but current evidence supports testing Ervebo in outbreak response. The recommendation comes amid ongoing outbreak response in the DRC and international efforts to limit spread and boost vaccination and prevention measures.

triage.headline_ja: WHOがコンゴでのエボラ対策として臨床試験に「エルベボ」ワクチンの組み入れを推奨
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中のブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス流行に対し、WHOがワクチン臨床試験を推奨するなど公衆衛生上重大かつ異常な事態であり、国際的な対応が継続しているためフルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事はブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス（Bundibugyo virus）に関するもので、ザイール型用ワクチン「エルベボ」の交差防御効果を検証する臨床試験をWHOが推奨している内容。国際的拡大や渡航制限に関する具体的記載はないため不明とした。

article.articleHeadline: 'That Escalated Fast': Swara Bhasker Admitted To Hospital Due To Dengue
article.articleSummary: Swara Bhasker and Avika Gor have both been hospitalised with dengue. Swara Bhasker announced on Instagram that she has been 'dengue-fied and hospitalised.' Avika Gor’s husband Milind Chandwani posted that she was admitted Thursday night after a fever lasting five days, with temperatures of 103-104°F; he noted she completed two days of a project prior to admission and teased the release of her new song Bukhaar. The piece mentions Swara’s work on the TV show Pati Patni Aur Panga and Avika’s ongoing project. Both cases are current as of 2026-08-08 and are presented via social-media updates from the celebrities and family; no fatalities are reported in the article.

article.articleHeadline: Over 200 mithuns die in foot-and-mouth disease in Arunachal
article.articleSummary: Over 200 mithuns have died from a foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak in Dibang Valley, Arunachal Pradesh. Acheso village accounts for the majority of deaths (>90), followed by Angrim (>50) and ALG (3); infections also detected in Aropo and Gipulin. The district hosts about 3,925 mithuns. Veterinary teams have intensified field operations; a rapid response team will join containment, while another team will collect samples and conduct an epidemiological investigation to determine spread and source. A four-member department team has been deployed to assess outbreak extent and assist district authorities. Tezu's eastern zone issued a high-alert advisory, urging eastern districts to boost surveillance, regulate animal movement, improve bio-security, vaccinate, and ensure prompt sampling. Fresh FMD cases have been reported from Yangfo, East Kameng and Damro in Upper Siang; Siang district urges owners to report suspected infections. Some affected animals had not been vaccinated previously; a statewide advisory followed outbreaks in East Kameng, Pakke-Kessang, Papum Pare and Dibang Valley.

triage.notes: 対象は家畜（ミトゥン）の口蹄疫であり、ヒトの感染症ではない。地元獣医当局が対応中であり、州レベルでの家畜衛生管理事案としての扱いが適切。

article.articleHeadline: Pemkab Penajam latih tim K3-tenaga medis proyek IKN cegah DBD
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Penajam Regency Government trains the OSH team for medical personnel in the IKN project to prevent dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: Penajam Paser Utara, Kalimantan Timur, Indonesia, trains OSH teams and IKN construction medical personnel to prevent dengue fever (DENV). Noted 24 dengue cases among IKN workers; as of 2026, 113 dengue cases are recorded in Penajam Paser Utara across Penajam, Waru, Babulu, and Sepaku (IKN area). Training covers identifying mosquito larvae and distributing larvicides; ongoing coordination with the IKN Authority supports prevention across all construction segments. Open-water containers during the dry season foster Aedes aegypti breeding, and vector control through mosquito nest eradication (PSN) remains the most effective method to interrupt transmission. Historical totals show 1,484 dengue cases in 2024 and 384 in 2025, with a goal to keep annual cases below 200.

triage.headline_ja: プナジャム県、IKNプロジェクトの労働安全衛生チーム・医療従事者にデング熱予防訓練を実施

triage.notes: 地方自治体主導の予防的訓練活動に関する記事であり、症例数は減少傾向にある。デング熱は東南アジアの風土病でありIHR基準には該当しない。継続的なベクター対策としての通常業務報道。

article.articleHeadline: Wamenkes Puji Kemajuan RSUP Wahidin Makassar dalam Penanganan TBC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deputy Health Minister Praises Wahidin Makassar Central General Hospital's Progress in TB Treatment
article.articleSummary: TB control progress at RSUP Dr. Wahidin Sudirohusodo in Makassar, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, was highlighted by Deputy Health Minister Benyamin Paulus Octavianus during a TB control visit on 2026-08-08. The hospital reported 1,517 suspected TB cases in 2026 to date (Q1: 517, Q2: 689, Q3: 311). Of these, 1,439 underwent bacteriological or clinical assessment; 151 were bacteriologically confirmed as TB susceptible (SO), and 135 were diagnosed clinically. Seven cases were bacteriologically confirmed as drug-resistant TB (RO). Treatment has been initiated for 227 SO and 7 RO patients. Among those, 5 SO and 3 RO patients have been cured after completing full treatment. The visit aimed to strengthen case finding, laboratory capacity, and human resources to support TB referral services across Indonesia’s eastern region, underscoring ongoing TB control efforts in South Sulawesi.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue Decoded: Symptoms, Myths, Prevention & Life-Saving Tips | Health Matters | Dengue News
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is explored in Dengue Decoded: Symptoms, Myths, Prevention & Life-Saving Tips, a Health Matters episode by CNN-News18. As dengue remains a major seasonal health concern, the video delineates early warning signs and symptoms—fever, body pain, headache—and explains when medical attention is needed. It clarifies how dengue spreads via mosquito bites and outlines practical steps to reduce exposure at home and in the neighborhood. The program also debunks common myths, emphasizing the risks of misinformation. Viewers are advised on precautions families can take during dengue season. The segment stresses that the video provides general health information and does not replace professional medical advice. Published 2026-08-08.

article.articleHeadline: More than 300 children have died from Ebola since start of DRC outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Ituri, DRC, continues to spread, with Ituri as the epicentre. By 8 August 2026, total confirmed cases exceed 4,000 with 1,850 deaths; more than 300 children have died, children about a quarter of cases but nearly a third of deaths. Access to essential health services in hardest-hit areas has fallen by more than 40% as fear of infection grows. Maternal deaths in Ituri have nearly doubled, with about six women dying weekly from childbirth complications; Ebola infection during pregnancy remains linked to almost universal fetal loss. The WHO TAC on Vaccine Research has recommended a clinical trial in the DRC to evaluate Ervebo against Bundibugyo virus; Ervebo is the only licensed Ebola vaccine. The WHO and partners plan to start the trial soon. Some 13,000 community workers have reached over 2.4 million people and carried out 500,000 household visits to counter misinformation and boost detection.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでのエボラ流行、発生以来300人以上の子どもが死亡
triage.triage_reason: 確定症例4,000人超、死亡1,850人に達する大規模な進行中のエボラ流行であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的懸念（WHO主導の臨床試験計画）が明確に確認できる。
triage.notes: WHOがEbola Bundibugyo株に対するワクチン臨床試験を計画中であり、既存のErveboワクチンの有効性が問われる新たな展開。医療アクセス低下や妊産婦死亡増加など二次的被害も深刻。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : Ebola tue plus de 300 enfants, l'ONU alerte sur une crise sanitaire majeure
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Ebola kills more than 300 children, the UN warns of a major health crisis.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo continues to claim lives, with UNICEF reporting over 300 child deaths since the outbreak began; children account for about a quarter of confirmed cases and roughly a third of deaths. Health service access has deteriorated, with essential services down more than 40% in hard-hit areas due to fear of infection. In Ituri province, maternal mortality has nearly doubled, averaging about six pregnancy-related deaths per week, and Ebola infection during pregnancy remains linked to high fetal loss. The World Health Organization is accelerating vaccination efforts and planning an Ervebo vaccine trial in the DRC, the only approved Ebola vaccine. As of August 2026, total cases exceed 4,000 and deaths exceed 1,850. Prevention outreach includes 13,000 community health workers, reaching over 2.4 million people and conducting 500,000 home visits to counter misinformation and encourage care.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:エボラで子ども300人以上死亡、国連が重大な公衆衛生危機を警告
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱が4,000人超の症例・1,850人超の死亡に達し、IHR基準の複数該当・国際機関の関与も明確なためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 国連・WHO・UNICEFが関与する大規模アウトブレイクであり、既に国際的な支援体制が構築されている状況。

article.articleHeadline: 치명률 45% '공포의 바이러스'...수도까지 번질라 '초비상' [글로벌 pick]
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 45% fatality rate, 'the dreaded virus'... could spread even to the capital, 'extreme emergency' [Global Pick]
article.articleSummary: As of August 5, 2026, Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak has 4,053 cumulative cases and 1,850 deaths (case fatality 45.7%). It is the largest outbreak in DRC’s history, surpassing 2018–2020 figures, and the second-largest since 2014–2016 West Africa. The epidemic is centered in Ituri province and northeastern provinces, with no wide geographic diffusion reported yet. A ship bound for Kinshasa carried a suspected case: a 32-year-old man from Mongala who developed fever and diarrhea, died after disembarking in Pimu; the vessel traveled 1,700 km and was halted 65 km from Kinshasa at Maluku. 300 passengers were screened; seven with fever or headache tested negative. Kinshasa port surveillance has intensified. Frontline workers face wage arrears; WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged support. Vaccination against Zaire ebolavirus is being deployed in Ituri and North Kivu; Bundibugyo vaccine trials underway; remdesivir discussed to expand antiviral use. Civil conflict hampers access and tracing.

triage.headline_ja: 致死率45%「恐怖のウイルス」…首都にまで拡大か「超非常事態」【グローバルピック】
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行(致死率45.7%)が拡大中で、首都キンシャサへの拡散懸念があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するため。
triage.notes: 史上最大規模のDRCエボラ流行。首都キンシャサ行きの船に疑い症例があり水際対策が強化されている。内戦により対応が困難。WHOも支援を要請。

article.articleHeadline: 專家：香港正受新冠等"三疫夾擊" | 電訊
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Experts: Hong Kong is under a triple-epidemic attack, including COVID-19 | Telecom News
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong is experiencing a triple-epidemic of COVID-19, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The city has recorded the year's first pediatric death from influenza. A clinical associate professor of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at The University of Hong Kong stressed the death is an isolated case and should not diminish vaccine confidence. With a vaccination program in operation for six months, waning antibody levels and individual health factors can influence protection. By the end of July, the Centre for Health Protection reported 12 children infected with influenza who developed severe complications. Although it is summer holidays, group activities continue to fuel transmission, and many children seek care at public hospitals and private clinics. Influenza cases have not yet peaked. Public health guidance urges basic precautions: wearing masks, diligent hand hygiene, and careful hygiene during travel.

article.articleHeadline: बच्चों को बचाएं बरसाती बीमारियों से (Protect children from monsoon-related illnesses)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Protect children from monsoon-related illnesses
article.articleSummary: During the monsoon, children face increased risk of infectious illnesses as their immune systems are relatively weak. Fungal infections commonly develop in damp conditions, especially between toes and fingers, due to prolonged contact with water; treatment involves applying antifungal cream and thorough drying. Boils (furuncles) arise from moisture‑loving bacteria and are treated with topical antibiotic cream. Conjunctivitis, or pink eye, spreads quickly in rainy weather; prevention centers on teaching hygiene and keeping infected children away. Malaria rises as standing water increases mosquito breeding; protection includes full‑sleeve clothing and topical repellent when outdoors and eliminating water pools around the home. Cholera also spreads via contaminated water and food; ensure adequate hydration and careful food and drink choices during the season. Extra care tips emphasize breathable clothing, washing with soap to remove residues, avoiding soaking in rain, and wearing sandals to keep feet dry.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization warns of an unprecedented acceleration of the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo | Libya Observer
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization warns of an unprecedented acceleration of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the outbreak extending beyond Ituri Province in the northeast. The 17th DRC Ebola outbreak has recorded 3,973 confirmed cases over 80 days, surpassing the 2018 record of 3,411, with deaths over 1,800 and about 776 recoveries (official figures may undercount). Approximately 84% of cases are in Ituri, which accounts for about 85% of the latest 99 new infections, and the outbreak has spread to five provinces. Delays in case detection and cases outside known transmission chains hinder containment. The surge is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no licensed vaccine or approved therapy. WHO warns that ongoing multi‑province spread could complicate containment unless surveillance, treatment capacity, and response efforts are accelerated.

article.articleHeadline: Bệnh viêm phổi Legionella do điều hòa bẩn: Nguy hiểm tiềm ẩn trong Mùa hè 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Legionella pneumonia caused by dirty air conditioning: Hidden dangers in the Summer of 2026.
article.articleSummary: Legionnaires' disease due to Legionella pneumophila linked to dirty air conditioning hospitalized a 78-year-old woman in Hangzhou, China during Summer 2026 after months of an unclean domestic AC. She developed prolonged fever, severe cough, and right-lung consolidation on CT; initial tests showed modest inflammation and cephalosporin therapy failed to resolve fever. Bronchoscopy and lavage confirmed Legionella pneumophila; symptoms improved after switching to appropriate antibiotics. Legionella, a Gram-negative bacterium, thrives in natural and artificial water systems and can colonize AC components—condensate trays, filters, ducts, and cooling towers—especially after long disuse. Early signs resemble flu or ordinary pneumonia, risking delayed diagnosis. High-risk groups include the elderly, those immunocompromised, with chronic lung disease, diabetes, or heart disease. A Beijing-Shenzhen survey found 88% of home evaporator coils exceeded bacterial standards, with 84% mold above safe levels, underscoring clean AC as a public health issue.

article.articleHeadline: AIIMS-Bhubaneswar plans advanced TB testing pilot in two Odisha districts
article.articleSummary: On 8 August 2026, AIIMS Bhubaneswar plans a two-district pilot of advanced tuberculosis testing in Odisha to assess feasibility of deploying sophisticated diagnostics across the state's public health system. The plan emerged from a two-day National Conclave and Policy Dialogue on Tuberculosis in Bhubaneswar, attended by policymakers, NTEP officials, scientists and clinicians. The initiative emphasizes strengthening TB diagnosis, surveillance and research toward a TB-Mukt Bharat, with Universal Drug Susceptibility Testing (UDST) and early detection of drug resistance highlighted by Odisha Assembly Speaker Surama Padhy. Health Minister Mukesh Mahaling welcomed collaboration with AIIMS Bhubaneswar and stakeholders to evaluate feasibility, affordability and scalability of genotypic testing and molecular diagnostics. AIIMS Executive Director Dr. Ashutosh Biswas underscored focus on TB research, genomics and evidence-based policy, with findings from the pilot guiding wider implementation in eastern India.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Environmental Surveillance of Três Passos participates in training on equipment used in the fight against arboviral diseases - Três Passos News
article.articleSummary: Três Passos, Brazil strengthens arboviral surveillance by training municipal environmental health staff in field-control equipment for Aedes aegypti and dengue. On August 5–6, 2026, Endemic Control Agents Adriane Schmitz, Fabiane Amaral, Laudecir Kirsten, and Elias Morais attended a Technical Training organized by the 2nd Regional Health Coordination (2ª CRS) in partnership with the State Center for Health Surveillance (CEVS), the Frederico Westphalen Municipal Health Department, and Agrocontinental. The training, held at the Frederico Westphalen Exposition Park, covered theoretical and practical use of equipment for arbovirus field actions, including motorized ULV equipment, the BRi battery, and heavy ULV gear, with hands-on sessions to improve application, maintenance, and operation. This initiative supports ongoing capacity building to enhance dengue and other arboviral disease prevention and control in the municipality, protecting public health.

article.articleHeadline: WHO recommends Ervebo vaccine for clinical trial against Ebola
article.articleSummary: WHO recommends prioritizing Ervebo, the only licensed Ebola vaccine, for inclusion in a randomized clinical trial to address the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Preliminary animal data suggest possible cross-protection, but vaccine effectiveness against the circulating Ebola virus remains unproven in humans. The WHO said vaccinating contacts of infected individuals did not raise safety concerns, while acknowledging that a vaccine specifically targeting Ebola remains the preferred long-term option. The outbreak is spreading rapidly in the DRC, with the death toll exceeding 1,800 as of August 8, 2026, and the pace beginning to outstrip current response efforts. This step aims to bolster immediate response through a trial while continuing broader surveillance and containment measures.

article.articleHeadline: Parents urged to vaccinate children amid flu, Covid-19 and RSV infection cases
article.articleSummary: As of 8 August 2026, Hong Kong faces a triple threat from influenza, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), with the summer flu season still high and not yet peaking. Despite ongoing transmission, there is no sign of a decline in flu activity, and officials have not yet seen a clear peak timing. Covid-19 and RSV cases are also running at high levels. Dr Mike Kwan Yat-wah, honorary clinical associate professor in the University of Hong Kong’s paediatrics and adolescent medicine department, warned that Hong Kong and neighbouring areas are under a triple attack from these pathogens. The city recorded its first pediatric death from influenza this year about four days prior. He urged parents to vaccinate children who have not yet done so.

article.articleHeadline: Expert: Triple-virus outbreak strikes HK, with peak still to come
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong is contending with a 'triple epidemic' of COVID-19, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, says Kwan Yat-wah, president of the Asian Society for Paediatric Infectious Diseases. The surge strains the healthcare system as the influenza season has not peaked. Public health guidance urges vigilance, masking, and frequent handwashing, with travel hygiene and holiday group activities potentially fueling spread. A seven-year-old boy died from influenza A—Hong Kong's first pediatric influenza fatality this year. He developed cold symptoms July 27, fever Aug 1, and deteriorated Aug 3 before dying Aug 4; influenza A with shock and encephalopathy was diagnosed. Preliminary CHP findings show he had received the 2025/26 seasonal vaccine and had no travel history, suggesting waning antibodies about six months after vaccination. To widen protection, authorities will expand the family doctor vaccine procurement pilot for 2026/27 from 100,000 to 300,000 doses; Kwan urges stronger procurement and public education to boost coverage.

article.articleHeadline: Point Santé : 4000 cas d'Ebola en RDC et le choléra progresse en Afrique centrale
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health Update: 4,000 Ebola Cases in the DRC and Cholera Is Spreading in Central Africa.
article.articleSummary: As of August 7, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 3,973 confirmed Ebola cases and more than 1,850 deaths across 51 health zones in five provinces, with Ituri bearing ~90% of cases and Bunia among the hardest hit. Between August 4–5, 99 new cases and 52 deaths were recorded; contact tracing stands at 75%, below the 95% target. Bunia’s treatment-center occupancy reached 139%. A WHO/Africa CDC mission (Aug 4–5) urged stronger community engagement, 95% contact follow-up, and rapid payments for frontline workers. The United States added $242 million on August 5 for Ebola response and preparedness in DRC, Uganda, and neighbors, within a larger UN package; travel advisories remain. Saudi Arabia suspended entry from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. Cholera spreads in Africa, with Cameroon reporting 800+ cases and 25 deaths as of July 28; Minawao camp houses 81,000 people, over capacity. Chad (239/13) and Central African Republic (720/46) are affected; climate change is cited as amplifying outbreaks; Institut Pasteur de Tunis was named Africa CDC North Africa environmental-surveillance hub.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, l'epidemia corre più veloce dei soccorsi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, the epidemic is outpacing the rescue efforts.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, continues to outpace the response. As of 4 August, 3,973 confirmed cases and 1,801 deaths have been reported; 776 recoveries in 51 health zones. About 90% of infections are in Ituri, centered on Bunia, with only 75% of contacts traced. Hospitals are stretched: 674 patients hospitalized and North Kivu centers at 139% capacity. Investigations indicate virus circulation in Mongbwalu since January, four months before official acknowledgment. Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) is being considered in a randomized trial despite targeting Ebola Zaire and not Bundibugyo; Bundibugyo-specific ChAdOx1 BDBV is in early trials. No travel restrictions are advised; emphasis on rapid diagnosis, contact tracing, beds, ambulances, and laboratories.

Speaking at the valedictory of a two-day TB conclave and policy dialogue hosted by AIIMS Bhubaneswar, she highlighted Universal Drug Susceptibility Testing (UDST) as a key to improving treatment outcomes, reducing transmission, and strengthening the public health system. The gathering, which included NTEP officials, researchers and clinicians, emphasized TB-Mukt Bharat as a national movement and stressed the need for pilot initiatives using advanced genotypic testing to generate policy evidence. Odisha Health and Family Welfare Minister Mukesh Mahaling said the government aimed to implement evidence-based pilots assessing feasibility, affordability and scalability of advanced diagnostics, including in two Odisha districts, to reach rural, tribal and remote areas, with AIIMS Bhubaneswar pursuing genomics and diagnostics research to inform policy.

article.articleHeadline: Oxford Vaccine Group seeks volunteers for world-first Ebola trial
article.articleSummary: Oxford Vaccine Group in Headington, Oxford launches the world’s first Phase I trial of a vaccine against Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BD-Ebov) using the ChAdOx1 Ebola BDBV Vaccine. The push follows May 2026 WHO PHEIC after Bundibugyo virus cases were detected in the Democratic Republic of the Congo; no licensed vaccine exists for this strain. The study recruits healthy adults 18–55 for a year with up to 12 visits at the Headington site. Group 1 (10 participants) receives an initial dose plus a six‑month booster; Group 2 (40 participants) receives a single vaccine dose or saltwater placebo. Outcomes focus on safety and immune response, with blood tests and symptom logging. Reimbursements are up to £1,200 (Group 1) and £790 (Group 2). The group has a 30+ year track record, contributing to typhoid vaccines and the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, and trials worldwide. Keywords: vaccination, outbreak, public health measures.

She had a five-day history of high fever (103–104°F) before admission and has been in hospital since the previous night. Despite the fever, Gor completed a pending two-day shoot in one day and later travelled to Delhi for an advertisement shoot, returning to Mumbai where dengue was laboratory-confirmed. Her husband, Milind Chandwani, posted on Instagram detailing her dedication and requesting prayers for her recovery. The report confirms laboratory confirmation of dengue; no case counts or outcomes are provided. The incident highlights dengue in urban India, with Mumbai and Delhi cited in the timeline.

article.articleHeadline: 專家：香港正遭受「三疫夾擊」 勿輕忽流感 - 國際新聞 - PChome Online 新聞
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Experts: Hong Kong is under a "triple-epidemic" assault; do not underestimate the flu.
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong is experiencing a 'triple-epidemic' of COVID-19, influenza, and RSV, according to Professor Kwan, president of the Asian Society of Pediatric Infectious Diseases and honorary clinical associate professor at The University of Hong Kong’s Department of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine. A 7-year-old boy in Hong Kong recently died from influenza A infection with shock and encephalopathy, underscoring influenza’s ongoing danger. Professor Kwan says this unfortunate case highlights the need not to underestimate flu, as immune overreaction can cause rapid deterioration. The child had received an influenza vaccination, but the time since vaccination was relatively long, antibodies may have waned, and factors such as underlying conditions and potential antigenic drift in circulating strains should be considered. He emphasizes that influenza has not peaked yet and urges continued vigilance and vaccination to mitigate severe outcomes.

article.articleHeadline: L'OMS préconise un essai clinique contre Ebola avec le vaccin Ervebo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO recommends a clinical trial against Ebola with the Ervebo vaccine.
article.articleSummary: As of 8 August 2026, the World Health Organization recommends prioritizing a randomized clinical trial to evaluate the authorized Ebola vaccine Ervebo in the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak response. The Technical Advisory Group on prioritizing candidate vaccines concluded that preliminary data indicate Ervebo offers some cross-protection against Ebola, but its efficacy against the virus must be demonstrated. Using the vaccine to immunize individuals with known exposure raises no safety concerns, while the long-term option preferred is developing a vaccine specifically targeting the Ebola virus. Ebola transmits through contact with bodily fluids and causes hemorrhagic fever; over the past five decades, it has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa. This guidance, issued from Geneva, addresses the RDC crisis and aims to inform outbreak response and vaccination strategies.”}

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chikungunya; Preventive measures and symptoms
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya causes high fever, joint pain and swelling, headache, body aches, fatigue, and skin rashes. It is not spread person-to-person; transmission occurs only through bites of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Mosquitoes breed in standing water in flower pots, buckets, discarded tires, coolers, and other containers. After a bite, symptoms typically emerge about 4–8 days later (WHO). There is no specific antiviral treatment; management is supportive with rest, fluids, and paracetamol for fever and pain. Symptoms can resemble dengue. Preventive measures include dressing children in long sleeves, using nets and repellents, installing window screens, and weekly cleaning of water-holding containers. Remove standing water from balconies, gardens, coolers, and outdoor areas; keep doors and windows closed during peak mosquito times. Tamil Nadu reports rising chikungunya cases; Kerala has experienced past outbreaks.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: While strolling in the park, a stray dog licked her foot; toe paronychia requires rabies vaccination - International - Real-Time International
article.articleSummary: In Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China, a woman with toe paronychia was exposed to rabies after a stray dog licked her injured toe. At Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital, clinicians found a disrupted skin barrier at the licking site and pain on cleansing, classifying her as Category III rabies exposure. She was advised to receive rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) per protocol to halt viral spread. The report warns that rabies exposure is not limited to bites; saliva contact with broken skin can pose a high risk, even when wounds are not obvious. Guidelines require vaccination and RIG for Category III exposures, with prompt evaluation if skin integrity is uncertain. Rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear, but timely post-exposure prophylaxis markedly reduces risk. Do not rely on luck when encountering stray dogs or cats.

article.articleHeadline: WHO ta bukaci amfani da rigakafin Ebola na Ervebo a Kwango
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO has urged the use of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine in Kwango.
article.articleSummary: As of 8 August 2026, the World Health Organization is urging thorough trials of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Kwango province to determine whether it can protect against a more challenging, dangerous Ebola strain. The current outbreak continues to spread in the DRC. Animal studies indicate Ervebo may confer protection against Bundibugyo, the strain highlighted in Kwango. Official figures report more than 1,800 deaths and 4,053 confirmed cases linked to the outbreak. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the virus is spreading faster than containment measures can keep up with. The article focuses on evaluating Ervebo’s efficacy against Bundibugyo in Kwango and underscores the urgent need for continued surveillance and research to curb transmission.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United States imposes temporary travel restrictions on travelers arriving from countries affected by the Ebola virus.
article.articleSummary: The United States imposed temporary travel restrictions on travelers arriving from Uganda, South Sudan, and the Democratic Republic of Congo as a precaution to curb Ebola transmission. In the DRC, Ebola infections have risen to 4,053 cases with 1,850 deaths, the highest counts since the outbreak began, according to the DRC’s Public Health Institute and corroborated by WHO estimates. The outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, is expanding rapidly, with officials noting a pace not seen in the 2014 West Africa epidemic. The WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warns of swift spread, while Africa CDC Director-General John Kasia says the numbers likely reflect ongoing transmission and potential undetected cases. International partners continue surveillance, treatment, and containment efforts, though health worker strikes over pay are hampering response efforts.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: CG News: Malaria outbreak in North Chhattisgarh: from a one-and-a-half-year-old child to a 60-year-old elderly woman tested positive.
article.articleSummary: Malaria outbreak in North Chhattisgarh’s Bilaspur district, centered in Kota block after a woman’s death two days earlier. As of 8 August 2026, 39 people have tested positive, up from 31 confirmed by CMHO on 26 July and eight new cases since. In Udaipur Development Block’s forested, hilly villages, infections span from a 1.5-year-old child to a 60-year-old woman, with most patients belonging to tribal communities Pahadi Korwa and Pando. Heaviest impact areas include Mataringa, Kharranagar, Musar Dand, Mukna Pahad, Bara Pahad, Bakoi, and Semi Ghoghra. Treatment started per protocol; CMHO Dr P.S. Marko, SDM Ramraj Singh, and malaria supervisor Shravan Shrivas are overseeing field response. Ongoing surveillance extends to nearby Balrampur (Ramchandra­pur, Wadrafnagar, Kusmi) and Surajpur (Odgi, Bhaiyathan) districts during monsoon, with appeals to seek testing and use bed nets and eliminate standing water.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola virüsü salgını büyüyor! Ebola nedir, Türkiye'de var mı?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus outbreak is growing! What is Ebola, and is it in Turkey?
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo strain Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is expanding, with 3,973 confirmed cases and 1,801 deaths reported by 4 August 2026, per DRC's National Institute of Public Health; Africa CDC confirmed the total exceeding 4,000. The outbreak ranks as the second-largest on record, with weekly case and death totals eightfold and sixfold higher than those seen in the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic at its 11th week. Ebola Virus Disease is caused by Ebola virus, a Filoviridae RNA virus; incubation 2–21 days and patients are not infectious until symptoms appear. Common symptoms include fever, headache, muscle and joint pain, fatigue, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite; progression can involve bleeding. There is no licensed Ebola vaccine; treatment is supportive. No local or imported Ebola cases have been recorded in Turkey.

article.articleHeadline: OMS recomienda evaluar la vacuna Ervebo ante brote de ébola en RD del Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO recommends evaluating the Ervebo vaccine in response to an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: WHO’s Technical Advisory Group recommends prioritizing the Ervebo Ebola vaccine for inclusion in a randomized trial as part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak response. Ervebo is the only vaccine currently authorized against Ebola; animal data suggest possible cross-protection, but efficacy against the circulating virus remains to be proven. Safety concerns for vaccinating contacts of Ebola cases appear not to be known, with no new safety issues reported. A long-term goal remains a vaccine specifically tailored to the outbreak virus. As of August 8, 2026, WHO warned of accelerating transmission in DRC, with fatalities exceeding 1,800 and transmission outpacing response capacity. The evaluation aims to broaden tools for surveillance, prevention, and outbreak response while ongoing monitoring continues.

article.articleHeadline: JMC begins 3-month mosquito control drive in Jammu
article.articleSummary: Jammu Municipal Corporation launches a three-month city-wide mosquito-control drive from Aug 8 to Nov 10, 2026, across all 75 wards to curb dengue, chikungunya and malaria. The fogging and spraying program, guided by Health Officer Shahid Hussain, will run in phased rounds with early-morning fogging and post-4 pm thermal fogging daily. Last year in the Jammu region, dengue cases exceeded 1,100, including 460 in Jammu district, down from 1,876 the year before, a decline attributed to sustained anti-mosquito measures. Residents are urged to cooperate, eliminate standing water around homes, and keep surroundings clean to reduce breeding. The JMC recommends residents, especially the elderly and people with asthma or smoke allergies, stay indoors during thermal fogging and close doors/windows until fog dissipates, while inspecting coolers, water containers, tyres, drains, and other water-holding items.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rapid rise in viral fever cases among children as the weather changes.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-08, viral infections are surging among children in Saran district, Chhapra, India, with Sadar Hospital OPD registrations nearly doubling in the first two shifts and private clinics reporting about half of patients with viral fever. School-going children are most affected, presenting with high fever, cold, cough, and body aches after returning to class. Pediatrician Dr. Prabhakar Kumar links the rise to fluctuating weather and temperature shifts that may weaken immunity. Senior Dr. Sudhanshu Shekhar Mishra notes many families rely on home remedies, causing 2–4 days of weakness; fever persisting beyond two days warrants medical evaluation. Dengue, malaria, chikungunya, and typhoid testing remain ongoing at Sadar Hospital, but most patients test positive only for common viral infections, with no new dengue cases reported. Authorities urge sanitation and elimination of standing water to curb spread.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Ausbruch im Kongo: Experten befürchten Mutation des Virus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Outbreak in the Congo: Experts Fear Mutation of the Virus.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo persists, with 4,053 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,850 deaths by 6 August 2026. The Bundibugyo variant continues to drive transmission at about 75 new cases per day, and containment is challenged in Ituri Province due to weak infrastructure and rebel activity. Since mid-May 2026, most new infections and deaths are from the general population, not just known contacts; contact tracing stands at 75% vs a 95% target. WHO Chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and Africa CDC Director Jean Kaseya urged an urgent expansion of response measures, including better testing access for affected communities. Uganda’s efforts are highlighted as exemplary; authorities will study a possible mutation given the epidemic’s unprecedented scale. Relative to West Africa’s 2014–2016 outbreak, the current period shows eightfold more cases and sixfold more deaths over 12 weeks.

article.articleHeadline: पशुओं में खुरपका-मुंहपका का बढ़ा खतरा! पैर पटकना और मुंह से लार गिरना दिखे हो जाएं सावधान
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In animals, the risk of foot-and-mouth disease has increased! Be alert for stamping of the feet and drooling from the mouth.
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease risk is rising in Shivpuri, India, a highly contagious viral disease affecting cows, buffaloes, and other livestock. It is not seasonal and can spread at any time. Early signs include 1–2 days of fever, stamping or limping, hoof swelling, and mouth ulcers with drooling that may rupture, causing feeding difficulties. The disease can reduce milk production and overall productivity; recovered animals may stay weak, and pregnancy loss with potential long-term fertility impacts can occur in pregnant animals. Veterinary consultation is essential for diagnosis and treatment. Home care includes washing hooves with phenyl-containing water 2–3 times daily, applying fly-repellent ointment, and using neem and peepal bark decoctions for cleaning. Mouth ulcers should be cleaned with 1% alum solution under veterinary guidance. If multiple animals are affected, isolate sick animals, disinfect facilities, and provide soft green forage, avoiding dry fodder, after professional advice.

article.articleHeadline: للمرة الأولى منذ بدء التفشي.. إصابات إيبولا في الكونغو تتجاوز 4 آلاف حالة - الأسبوع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: For the first time since the outbreak began... Ebola infections in the Congo exceed 4,000 cases - The Week
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 4,000 cases for the first time since the outbreak began. The latest report from the DRC’s Institute of Public Health tallies 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths. The outbreak, which started in May, is described as the fastest-transmitting in history, with confirmed cases exceeding 4,000 and deaths above 1,800. By contrast, the West Africa outbreak of 2014–2016 in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone totaled over 28,000 cases. Ebola spreads to humans via contact with infected wildlife and then through direct contact with the blood, body fluids, contaminated tools, or surfaces. The incubation period is two to 21 days. Early symptoms include high fever, fatigue, headache, and muscle pains, potentially progressing to internal and external bleeding and multi-organ failure if untreated.

article.articleHeadline: വേദനയും വീക്കവും ചുവപ്പുനിറവും; വൃഷണത്തിലെ അണുബാധ, പരിശോധനകളും ചികിത്സയും
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pain and fever and redness; infection of the scrotum, tests and treatments.
article.articleSummary: Orchitis, a significant male-health issue, is an infection of the testicle described from Thalassery Mission Hospital, Kerala. Causes include bacteria, viruses (notably mumps), or epididymitis, with risk factors such as immunocompromised states, chronic urinary tract problems, or post-surgical complications. Symptoms are testicular pain and swelling (may involve one or both testes), redness and warmth, fever, and fatigue; urinary symptoms like pain, burning, or blood in urine may occur. Diagnostics encompass ultrasound to assess swelling and complications, urine and blood tests for infectious agents, and STI screening when sexual transmission is suspected. Treatment consists of antibiotics for bacterial cases and analgesics for pain; viral/mumps cases rely on supportive care. Long-term concerns include fertility potential, chronic pain, and social stigma, with psychological distress potentially delaying care. Most patients recover with timely treatment. (Reported from Thalassery Mission Hospital, Kerala.)

article.articleHeadline: Avika Gor Hospitalised Due to Dengue, Actress' Husband Milind Chandwani Shares Health Update (Watch Video)
article.articleSummary: Avika Gor hospitalised in India after being diagnosed with dengue. She had a fever of 103–104°F for five days before admission, during which she continued working, completing a two-day project shoot in one day and then travelling to Delhi for an advertisement shoot to avoid postponements for producers. Her husband Milind Chandwani posted that she underwent tests to rule out other infections, which were negative. From her hospital bed, Avika posted that her platelet counts provided a glimmer of hope as she awaits recovery and noted that her new song Bukhaar would release the same day. Avika Gor, who rose to fame on Balika Vadhu and later worked in Sasural Simar Ka and in Telugu and Hindi cinema, is currently receiving medical care in India.

article.articleHeadline: L'Ebola en RDC inquiète des étudiants à Moncton
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC worries students in Moncton.
article.articleSummary: Canada’s Public Health Agency announced on July 19 a temporary entry ban for any foreign traveler who has stayed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the previous 21 days, in effect until August 29, to reduce the risk of Ebola importation and spread. The DRC Ebola outbreak has reached 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths, AFP reported. The measures affect students from Université de Moncton who originate from the DRC, causing visa delays and separation from family, including a planned graduation visit to Toronto that could not proceed. Université de Moncton says there are no confirmed cases of current students unable to return and cannot yet confirm impacts on new admits. New Brunswick Community College reports about 70 candidate students affected, with options to defer admission or receive refunds.

article.articleHeadline: Service Above Self: Will malaria return to N. America?
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a global threat as the United States completed its withdrawal from WHO on Jan 22, 2026, cutting 18% of the agency’s resources and limiting access to international data. About 282 million people are infected annually, with 610,000 deaths, 75% of them under five. In Canada, roughly 488 imported malaria cases are recorded each year, mostly among travelers from endemic areas. Rotarians Against Malaria, a Rotary Global Action Group, has expanded elimination efforts, with Rotary Foundation funding the first Program of Scale in Zambia. WHO has approved two vaccines against liver-stage parasites; PlasProtecT, supported by Rotary partners in Australia and nearing clinical trials, can be freeze-dried for transport and targets parasites after they leave the liver. Ongoing challenges include insecticide resistance, funding cuts, conflicts, trade disruptions, displacement, vaccine resistance, and data-sharing limits, heightening risk to Canada and North America amid imported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Tuyên Quang khẩn trương khống chế bệnh viêm da nổi cục trên đàn bò
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tuyen Quang Province Urgently Contains Lumpy Skin Disease in Cattle
article.articleSummary: Lumpy skin disease (LSD) outbreaks in cattle in Tuyen Quang Province, Vietnam, affect 5 communes with 166 infected cattle across 126 households and 23 deaths requiring culling. In the last 3 days, new LSD cases emerged in Lùng Tám, Cán Tỷ, and Minh Tân (94 cases, 70 households). In Lùng Tám, LSD affects 75 cattle in 57 households, with 8 deaths and culling of about 1,560 kg; authorities deployed rapid-response teams, disinfection, insect control, veterinary treatment guidance, and farm hygiene measures. Vaccination is advancing: 3,700 vaccine doses allocated for 2026; by 8 Aug, 920 doses have been administered in Lùng Tám (920 cattle), and nationwide in Minh Sơn (2,555 doses; 84.8% of herd), Thắng Mố (1,000; 20%), plus 920 in Lùng Tám (21.1%). Total 3,145 doses delivered in new outbreak areas. Officials call for vaccination coverage of 80–100% and strict controls on animal movement, sales, and slaughter.

article.articleHeadline: 香港七岁童染流感病逝 专家：三疫夹击须警惕
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A seven-year-old in Hong Kong dies after contracting influenza; experts warn of a triple-epidemic threat.
article.articleSummary: Seven-year-old boy in Hong Kong, vaccinated against influenza, died after contracting influenza A (H3) and rapidly developing encephalopathy. This marks the city’s first pediatric influenza death of the year. Guan Rihua, president of the Asian Society of Pediatric Infectious Diseases, called the case isolated and urged continued confidence in influenza vaccination, noting that waning antibodies after six months or underlying immune issues can lead to severe illness even after vaccination. The H3 strain is reported to progress to severe disease quickly, with some patients deteriorating within a day, including hypotension and multi-organ inflammation with brain involvement. Samples are being sent to university labs to check for major genetic mutations or antigenic changes. Since late June, Hong Kong entered the flu season; by end‑July there were 12 pediatric influenza cases with severe complications. In addition to flu, hospitalizations of children with COVID-19 and RSV are rising; parents should seek medical care for persistent high fever, lethargy, poor feeding, or reduced urination, rather than rely on rapid tests, as schools reopen and travel peaks.

triage.headline_ja: 香港で7歳児がインフルエンザに感染し死亡、専門家は「三重流行」への警戒を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 香港で季節性インフルエンザ（H3）による小児死亡例が発生し、急速な脳症進行や遺伝子変異の可能性が調査中であり、COVID-19・RSVとの同時流行懸念もあるため、続報確認とリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 香港（中国特別行政区）での事例のため、対象国リストのChinaに分類。H3株の遺伝子変異の有無について大学研究室で検査中であり、今後の変異情報や重症例増加の動向を注視する必要がある。

article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is accelerating, with health officials warning that cases are doubling in some of the most affected areas. The article notes rising case numbers as transmission widens across the DRC. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus met in Kinshasa with President Félix Tshisekedi to discuss the crisis and response efforts. The excerpt does not provide specific national case or death totals. The outbreak remains centered in the Congo, with Kinshasa serving as the coordination backdrop for high-level discussions, reflecting ongoing international concern and the imperative for continued surveillance and mitigation of transmission in affected regions.

article.articleHeadline: 'That escalated fast': Swara Bhasker hospitalised after being diagnosed with dengue
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-08, two Indian actors are hospitalized after dengue. Swara Bhasker revealed she tested positive for dengue and is admitted, posting on Instagram, “Well that escalated fast. Dengue-fied and hospitalised!” Avika Gor was also hospitalised after a dengue diagnosis; her husband Milind Chandwani said she endured a five-day fever of 103–104°F, continued a two-day project shoot, then was admitted last night. Bhasker, who last appeared in the TV show Pati Patni Aur Panga, has no films announced. Gor’s upcoming projects were not specified. The report underscores dengue infections and hospitalisation in India, highlighting high fever, temporary work disruption, and subsequent medical care for both celebrities.

article.articleHeadline: RT-Duits: Ebola-Ausbruch im Kongo: Experten befürchten Mutation des Virus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: RT-Duits: Ebola outbreak in the Congo: Experts fear mutation of the virus.
article.articleSummary: As of 6 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 4,053 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,850 deaths, with an average of 75 new infections per day, driven by the Bundibugyo variant. The Ituri province bears the brunt amid instability and rebel activity that hamper response infrastructure. Experts fear potential mutation of the virus, underscoring urgency. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and Africa CDC Director Jean Kaseya urged an immediate expansion of outbreak control measures after visits to DRC and neighboring Uganda. Contact tracing coverage is about 75%, well short of the 95% target, complicating efforts to interrupt transmission chains. Uganda’s response is highlighted by WHO as exemplary, while concerns persist about capabilities to implement measures in eastern DRC.

article.articleHeadline: Swara Bhasker Hospitalised With Dengue: 5 Symptoms You Should Keep An Eye For In Monsoon
article.articleSummary: Swara Bhasker has been hospitalized for dengue in India, posting an Instagram update showing an IV drip. Actress Avika Gor was also recently hospitalized for dengue, with her husband Milind Chandwani confirming via video. The piece notes dengue is now a year-round challenge in India, driven by warmer temperatures that accelerate mosquito reproduction and transmission; heavy rainfall and prolonged dry spells create breeding sites in standing water and stored water. In the last five years, India officially reported about 968,000 dengue cases, peaking in 2023 with 289,235 cases and 485 deaths. Reported symptoms include fever, joint and muscle pain, headache and eye pain, nausea/vomiting, and rash. The article mentions signs of severe dengue to watch for, though those specific indicators are not listed in the excerpt.

article.articleHeadline: Exclusive: Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh And Sikkim Carry India's Kala-azar Burden
article.articleSummary: Kala-azar (Visceral Leishmaniasis) burden persists in India across Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, and Sikkim, based on June–December month-wise health ministry data for 2023–2025. Bihar remains the worst-affected: 2023—170 cases/0 deaths; 2024—167/5; 2025—105/0, with monthly peaks in Aug 2023 (36), Jun 2024 (42) and Jul 2025 (24). Jharkhand is second: 77 (2023), 94 (2024), 80 (2025), all with zero deaths; peaks of 21 (Sept 2023), 19 (Dec 2024), 17 (Jun 2025) indicate year-round but low-level transmission. West Bengal reports 11 (2023), 20 (2024, 1 death), 23 (2025), with most infections August–October. Uttar Pradesh records 8 cases annually (2023–2025) with deaths 0, 1, and 3 respectively, and no prolonged outbreak. Sikkim is listed among burden states, though the article provides no year-wise counts.
